locator.text: Display 149.4, p. 149, in the proof of Proposition B.3

evidence: paper: S_q \ge \Lambda L \chi - W_* - 10h - C\chi - C_{\sigma_*}\sqrt{\chi} - C/\Lambda.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The display is an intermediate lower bound for S_q with the error terms exhibited (-Cχ - C_{σ_*}√χ - C/Λ) and the axis contribution split as -W_* - 10h. No declaration was found stating it: searching the index for any lower bound on `Sq h …` returned only the two 19/20-type bounds (`source_uniform_lower`, and the `source_lower` fields of `EntranceProfile` at NaturalEntrance.lean:1099 and of `Estimates` at NaturalExitBounds.lean:133), which are (B.17), the display's consequence, not the display. In place of the inequality the Lean proves the exact identity `Sq_coefficient_identity` / `Sq_reconstruction` (line 516): S_q = LΛχ + remainder, with every error the paper bounds left inside `sourceRemainder` and then controlled by compactness plus the uniform coefficient-space limit. The axis part differs in packaging and is slightly stronger in Lean: the paper bounds -W_* > 2.8 and |h(1-2ηU)| ≤ 10h ≤ .1 separately, giving -W_* - 10h > 2.7, whereas `base_source_lower` states the combined quantity -W - h(1-2ηU) > 2.9 on all of [-1,1]. The paper's parenthetical 'no division by χ is used near a zero of H_*' is matched in spirit by the Lean remainder, in which the clamp max(1/8, φ) and not χ sits in every denominator. Surrounding result (B.17) is proved, so this is a route difference, not a gap in the conclusion.
